what_worked: Strong central thesis—pricing model and buyer type matter more than category—carried consistently through every slide.
fix_next: Analysis stays at the top-earner anecdote level; use dataset-wide medians, distributions, and missingness disclosure to substantiate the pricing-model claim.
verdict: Coherent narrative thesis, but thin on dataset-wide evidence and accuracy.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: Shows only 9 companies in top list; top-10 share (~49.6%) never stated. Slide 5: Claims pricing model is 'consistently the biggest single driver of revenue-per-account in the dataset' — no systematic evidence from the 1,000-row dataset supports this; it is inferred from ~7 hand-picked cases. Slide 6: States AI-tagged companies range '$0 to $575K' — the highest AI-category revenue is part of the $2.36M total but the single-company max needs verification; $575K appears fabricated or misread. Slide 4: Claims '6 of top 8 earners are B2B' — the actual audience_type field has 288 missing values and the B2B/B2C median multipliers (~2.35x/2.30x) are nearly identical, undermining the strong causal framing presented.

evidence.insight: The pricing-model spectrum (slide 5) and revenue-per-user calculations (slide 3) show genuine analytical thinking, but insights are derived from only 7-9 cherry-picked companies rather than the full dataset. No medians, distributions, or category-level comparisons are offered.
evidence.narrative: Clear five-part structure with a consistent thesis ('pricing and buyer > category') that builds logically from leaderboard → subscribers → B2B/B2C → pricing → domain rating → summary. The closing slide lands the argument well.
evidence.framing: No mention of dataset size (1,000 rows), missingness (241-288 missing across key fields), zero-revenue companies (216), or total revenue ($15.6M). Audience is implied but never stated. No limitations section. A cold reader cannot assess how representative the analysis is.
evidence.accuracy: Revenue-per-user calculations on slide 3 are internally consistent with the bar chart values. However, the AI revenue range ($575K max) appears incorrect. The central pricing-model claim is asserted from ~7 examples without systematic dataset evidence. No denominators, sample sizes, or statistical measures are provided anywhere. The B2B vs B2C framing ignores that median revenue multiples are nearly identical (~2.3x) across the full dataset.
evidence.visual: Clean, professional design with consistent color palette, good hierarchy, and readable charts. Bar charts on slides 2-3 are well-labeled. The pricing spectrum on slide 5 is an effective conceptual diagram. Slight concern: slide 6 uses a bar chart for only 5 cherry-picked DR values, which could mislead about the DR-revenue relationship across the full dataset.
evidence.ai_slop: The deck avoids generic filler and consulting buzzwords. The pricing spectrum diagram (slide 5) is conceptually useful but not grounded in dataset columns — it reads as an externally-sourced framework imposed on a few examples rather than emerging from data analysis.
